Track the 2026-05-19 physics-collision slice even though it was started and completed in one session. Mike's CI Training playtest showed c038/B-339 improved top/bottom jump collision, but the player could still jump sideways through overhead solid blockers and could get stuck above a doorway or inside a new blocker. Dynamic couch collision looked correct after moving the couch.

Legacy notes: Code/build slice completed 2026-05-19. Root cause: player airborne movement applied horizontal X/Z first, then bwalkUpdateVertical() only swept move=(0, verticalDelta, 0), so side-entry during a jump could bypass the side plane before vertical clamping. Fix: src/game/bondwalk.c adds bwalkClampAirborneSideEntry(), an upward diagonal capsuleSweep() from bondprevpos to the already-applied X/Z plus verticalDelta; on hit it rolls X/Z back to the safe fraction and clamps/kills upward velocity for ceiling-class hits. Test fixture now covers side-wall rendered triangles. Verification passed: scoped git diff --check, b350side tests target, focused [physics][jump] (99 assertions / 4 cases), and b350side all-target build. Manual CI Training retest remains the closure gate.
2026-05-22 B-367 follow-up: Mike reported the jumping player still clips into walls, ceilings, or corners. Root cause was the remaining horizontal half of the movement-order split: apex/descent lateral motion still committed through the legacy cylinder path before any capsule mesh repair ran. Fix: bwalkClampAirborneLateralEntry() now runs immediately after horizontal movement and before speed correction when airborne, uses the collision-owned capsule mesh sweep from bondprevpos, rolls X/Z back on wall/ceiling/corner hits, and ignores floor-class hits. Verification passed: focused [physics][jump] (105 assertions / 4 cases) and jump367 all-target build. Manual retest remains the closure gate.
Priority pass 2026-05-20: Collision critical path. Manual CI Training retest remains the gate before broader gameplay-stability work is treated as reliable.

item.title: Legacy decision for c081: Queue Match stores/cycles an array of match-start settings with a host-visible queued-count badge (behavior is designed in the grammar doc)…
item.detail: Queue Match stores/cycles an array of match-start settings with a host-visible queued-count badge (behavior is designed in the grammar doc). The one open architectural axis: should the queue STATE be host-local or synced to all clients? This decides whether c081 needs a new SVC_QUEUE_STATE net message + a NET_PROTOCOL_VER bump.

options.label: Host-local queue (no net message)
options.tradeoff: Queue Match is a host-convenience feature; the host cycles settings as matches end and clients simply load whatever the next match is. Simplest to ship, no protocol change, fits the P3-deferred scope. The queued-count badge is host-screen-only; joined clients cannot see how many matches are queued or what is coming. No SVC_QUEUE_STATE, no protocol bump, no resync-path changes.

options.label: Networked queue (SVC_QUEUE_STATE + protocol bump)
options.tradeoff: Every player sees the queued count and upcoming settings, which suits organized/tournament play and matches the 'badge displays queued count' intent for all participants. Adds a new SVC_QUEUE_STATE message, a NET_PROTOCOL_VER increment (must update g_TestExpectedNetProtocolVer in tests/test_versions.cpp in the same change per the silent-bump guard), queue state in the resync path, and a larger test surface.

detail.from: Partial production proof now covers ordinary edited gameplay/audio/presentation, preserved-install restart, production Mod Manager disable/re-enable, exact pink/cyan source-to-render A/B, same-process valid replacement plus rejected-candidate rollback, and overlapping owner balance. The final owner receipt passes 40/40: an explicit second weapon owner raises the weapon/effect/SFX closure to ref=2, its release retains all three 2->1, and real Mod Manager checkbox/Apply input retires the remaining closure 1->0. B-1030 fixes the Apply modal style scope exposed by the first otherwise-green run; the rerun has no ImGui/style-stack diagnostics. Complete automation passes 54,992 assertions/998 cases plus native-source guard and all 27-family conformance. V-009 remains partial only because retained frames are not readable enough for pixel-level visual comparison and no real peer has distributed/replaced the edited archive. B-1031 proof tooling is under corrected reverification: the first live run disproved WorkingDirectory-only isolation because --portable resolves base/save from the canonical executable. The runner now keeps the stable canonical executable but passes each peer an explicit isolated --basedir/--savedir; corrected parser/build/focused coverage passes 26 assertions/2 cases; the real ENet receipt remains pending.

The final Needler peer path passes 87/87 from a client with no local package through SHA verification, transactional session-only admission, READY, exact nonzero arena session, runtime weapon 86 firing, catalog audio/gameplay commit, and world-renderer presentation. Random/meta propagation separately passes 34/34 with one concrete base:mp_skedar identity and session 1 on both peers. Full suite, native-source guard, all-family/Needler conformance, and unchanged final fingerprint pass.

2026-08-12 readable-output closure: B-1055/B-1056 prove the reported player-following white obstruction was the held public Needler authored 14x near the camera while the GLTF compiler dropped baseColorFactor. The regenerated archive uses scale 5 at (30,-18,-45), valid base colour reaches runtime vertices, and the ordinary client passes 21/21 with two inspected lower-right/unobstructed captures. B-1054 retains an additive outer flare but alpha-blends the authored-colour core; separate public-source pink and cyan archives each pass 46/46, exact authored/effective/render RGBA remains distinct, and inspected 700/900 ms captures show coloured fragments without a white bloom.

The Needler production and readable visual gates are complete. V-009 remains partial only because T-CATALOG-003 is still a partial Workbench dependency for the comprehensive live all-family three-ingress matrix.

Render-critical (g_ModelStates + firing path), B-801 live-unverifiable. Under the c3844 100%-parity umbrella.

item.detail: The 1.0 contract is a stable, complete PC base game plus usable Theater, not the earlier full Forge-platform milestone. Every shipped base-game system and accepted graph surface must be connected to production behavior, fail closed when authoritative source is invalid, and pass gameplay parity validation. Theater must record enough authoritative session data to reconstruct and play campaign and Combat Simulator sessions after process restart, with working save/list/load/playback and spectator camera controls. One deliberately small sample mod weapon must prove the public weapon graph/runtime/distribution/custom-match-slot seam. Forge map creation, map variants, broad creator/pipeline tooling, Studio, and Needler-specific feature polish are post-1.0.
evidence: Mike 2026-08-12: base game must be 100% properly implemented including graphs; Theater must save/load usable campaign and Combat Simulator replays; Forge maps/map variants and modding pipeline tooling may follow 1.0; Needler may be deferred in favor of a minimal custom-slot sample weapon.
item.resolution: Option A - Base game plus Theater. Base game implementation and every accepted graph surface must be complete; Theater must persist and replay campaign and Combat Simulator sessions; ship one minimal custom-slot sample weapon. Defer Forge maps/map variants, broad modding pipeline tooling, Studio, and Needler-specific polish until after 1.0.

item.title: Implement production Theater recording and replay for campaign and Combat Simulator
item.detail: A participant-snapshot recorder, replay reader, replay list, and shared spectator overlay exist, but they are not a usable match replay system. Current recording only samples SPECTATOR_SOURCE_LIVE participants, never emits THEATER_RECORD_MATCH_CONFIG, does not reconstruct a campaign or Combat Simulator stage/world, has no pause/seek/index, and cannot capture an ordinary local campaign or host match without a synthetic spectator path. Complete a versioned, bounded, fail-closed replay format and lifecycle that records authoritative match identity/configuration and enough ordered state/events/checkpoints to reconstruct campaign and Combat Simulator sessions after process restart. Playback must load the exact stage/catalog/manifest context, drive one shared spectator/Theater camera surface, support browse/play/pause/seek/stop, handle interrupted or corrupt files safely, preserve forward migration rules, and cleanly return to the menu. Include offline campaign, local Combat Simulator, and listen-host Combat Simulator where applicable; private/non-replayable data must not be serialized.

reason: Create the implementation lane required by D-004

item.title: Ship a minimal graph-backed sample mod weapon in custom match slots
item.detail: Author and ship a deliberately small public .pdmod/.pdweapon sample derived from a base gun, using either a three-round burst or an alternate projectile so its source-driven behavior is unmistakable without Needler-specific art or fidelity scope. The sample must use the production graph/runtime/catalog path, declare its typed dependencies, fail closed without fallback, install enabled in the appropriate sample/dev content policy, appear by permanent catalog identity in Match Setup custom weapon slots, save/reload with the setup, equip/fire in ordinary gameplay, and synchronize through listen-host manifest/session-catalog flow. It is a release seam test and documentation sample, not a broad creator-tool requirement.

reason: Create the minimal 1.0 sample weapon lane required by D-004

item.title: Validate complete base-game implementation and graph-backed gameplay parity
item.detail: Release gate for 100 percent proper base-game implementation. Audit every shipped campaign, Combat Simulator, co-op/Counter-Operative, menu, save, input, renderer, audio, physics, networking, and asset path for placeholders, disconnected code, silent fallback, or unsupported advertised behavior. Every accepted base-game graph surface, including scenario/AI/setup/objective/mission, weapon/projectile/entity, prop, effect, game-mode, and bot-profile graphs where present, must have a deliberate production consumer and gameplay-parity evidence. Explicit named native routines may remain as graph modules only when the graph intentionally selects them as the production implementation; hidden inactive graphs or fallback around authoritative graph source fail this gate. Validate all missions and representative mode/difficulty/device/network combinations with durable artifacts.

reason: Create the D-004 base-game completion gate

item.title: Validate campaign and Combat Simulator Theater save load and playback
item.detail: Record, stop, restart the ordinary client, list, load, and replay at least one campaign mission and one Combat Simulator match. Prove stage/config/catalog identity, participants/bots, objective and cutscene progression, doors/lifts/props/projectiles/effects, weapons, scores/timers, match end, and camera focus remain coherent enough to watch the session rather than only ghost participant transforms. Exercise play/pause/seek/stop, first-/third-person and free-fly controls, completed and interrupted recordings, corrupt/truncated/oversized/version-mismatched files, clean return to menu, and deterministic or explicitly bounded divergence checks. Include a listen-host Combat Simulator replay receipt if networked matches use a distinct authoritative capture path.

reason: Create the D-004 Theater production validation gate

item.title: Validate the sample mod weapon through custom match slots and gameplay
item.detail: From an ordinary release client, discover the shipped sample weapon through its public source, confirm that Match Setup can place it in every supported custom weapon slot by catalog identity, save/reload the setup, start a local Combat Simulator match, equip it, and observe its distinct three-round-burst or alternate-projectile behavior. Repeat through a two-client listen-host match with manifest/session-catalog synchronization and no client-local preinstall assumption where distribution is expected. Reject malformed or missing selected source without substituting a base weapon. Capture source identity, slot identity, gameplay behavior, network parity, clean shutdown, and the Needler obstruction/readability regression gate.

reason: Create the D-004 sample weapon production validation gate

Legacy notes: Code/build slice completed 2026-05-19. Root cause: player airborne movement applied horizontal X/Z first, then bwalkUpdateVertical() only swept move=(0, verticalDelta, 0), so side-entry during a jump could bypass the side plane before vertical clamping. Fix: src/game/bondwalk.c adds bwalkClampAirborneSideEntry(), an upward diagonal capsuleSweep() from bondprevpos to the already-applied X/Z plus verticalDelta; on hit it rolls X/Z back to the safe fraction and clamps/kills upward velocity for ceiling-class hits. Root cause was the remaining horizontal half of the movement-order split: apex/descent lateral motion still committed through the legacy cylinder path before any capsule mesh repair ran. Fix: bwalkClampAirborneLateralEntry() now runs immediately after horizontal movement and before speed correction when airborne, uses the collision-owned capsule mesh sweep from bondprevpos, rolls X/Z back on wall/ceiling/corner hits, and ignores floor-class hits. Verification passed: focused [physics][jump] (105 assertions / 4 cases) and jump367 all-target build. Manual retest remains the closure gate.

detail.from: Validated across all acceptance lanes. Production extraction completes cleanly and an induced typed-emitter failure exits 2, names the failing phase, blocks runtime-cache construction, and stops boot. Seven isolated installed-client processes reject corrupt public texture, vector font, animation, SFX, WAV voice, MP3 voice, and music source through their real consumers without ROM/native/loose fallback (47/47); B-1045 prevents malformed public fonts entering the ImGui atlas. B-1046 makes every PC JSON and binary MP setup writer candidate/flush/atomic-replace. Setup JSON/binary loads preserve live setup, match, handicap, weapon-set, and player-config state until complete validation. The exact client rejects four corrupt setup loads and preserves exact prior bytes across two injected post-write/pre-replace failures (17/17, six runtime cases). Final client/updater/tests builds, focused 84/7, full 56,544/1,026, native-source guard, scanner selftest, and 28-root/52-recursive all-27-family conformance pass under unchanged fingerprint c09c897808af837dd9db7d1c77c6d1a196e54340178a1146546ac9581fc8a385. Positive visual/audio/controller/creator/peer behavior remains owned by separate validation items.
detail.to: Reopened on 2026-08-13 after B-1068 contradicted the prior validated scope. Existing extraction and MP setup receipts remain valid, but Combat Simulator scenario JSON load is not fail-closed: it mutates live setup/player/bot state before complete validation, accepts ambiguous numeric fallback when typed fields are present but invalid, and crosses arena-index/stagenum domains. Return to validated only after candidate-first v3 parsing, bounded v1/v2 migration, exact rollback tests, and an ordinary-client save/load/start smoke.

detail.from: Historical c3746 Cohorts A, B, C, and the narrow E guards remain implemented: checked spawn-critical accessors, one spawn-with-weapon predicate, an exhausted allocation-time struct-field audit, loud body identity rejection, head-count lookup, and bot preload symmetry. The D overlay exists but is not complete. B-1064 owns exact typed identity, atomic player allocation, match participant preparation, chrbody publication, network stage application, and reconnect rollback. B-1065 owns engine-forced option ownership across start/end/cancel/disconnect/settings replacement and user-facing reads. B-1066 owns explicit stage-reuse reset defaults for weapon, previous/dual, ammo intent, passive mode, and jump state. Close with shared prepare/commit contracts, complete rollback, focused behavioral and negative-path tests, and source-frozen ordinary Campaign, Combat Simulator, transition, listen-host/client, disconnect, and reconnect receipts. B-1067 additionally owns prepared-roster drift between lobby commit and launch: exact decline restoration, remote option derivation, participant teams, typed mission identity, and catalog-before-readiness ordering. B-1069 owns the remaining post-freeze launch mutation: network mpStartMatch must consume the exact prepared roster/options/weapons/stage and cannot rerandomize, quick-team mutate, challenge-strip, or fallibly re-resolve after SVC_STAGE_START serialization. B-1070 owns the contradictory lobby-stage type boundary exposed by production smoke: introduce an exact mode-typed resolver for map versus arena, preserve campaign map-only semantics, and prove both wrong-domain rejection and ordinary two-client lifecycle. B-1071 removes the legacy positional CLC lobby handicap cache and makes each authenticated client settings the exact server-side roster authority, with a protocol bump and final SVC stage roster remaining authoritative. B-1071 remediation is source-connected but remains partial until focused builds/tests and a fresh ordinary two-client lifecycle pass under one source freeze. The first v55 ordinary run proved the positional field removal but exposed that transport-complete CLC_SETTINGS was still required. The current source now routes exact typed body/head identity, nonzero handicap, team, options, FOV, and name through a pure transactional codec before roster preparation; B-1071 remains partial until current-source focused/full tests and a source-frozen ordinary two-client lifecycle pass.

detail.from:
Historical c3746 Cohorts A, B, C, and the narrow E guards remain implemented: checked spawn-critical accessors, one spawn-with-weapon predicate, an exhausted allocation-time struct-field audit, loud body identity rejection, head-count lookup, and bot preload symmetry. The D overlay exists but is not complete. B-1064 owns exact typed identity, atomic player allocation, match participant preparation, chrbody publication, network stage application, and reconnect rollback. B-1065 owns engine-forced option ownership across start/end/cancel/disconnect/settings replacement and user-facing reads. B-1066 owns explicit stage-reuse reset defaults for weapon, previous/dual, ammo intent, passive mode, and jump state. Close with shared prepare/commit contracts, complete rollback, focused behavioral and negative-path tests, and source-frozen ordinary Campaign, Combat Simulator, transition, listen-host/client, disconnect, and reconnect receipts. B-1067 additionally owns prepared-roster drift between lobby commit and launch: exact decline restoration, remote option derivation, participant teams, typed mission identity, and catalog-before-readiness ordering. B-1069 owns the remaining post-freeze launch mutation: network mpStartMatch must consume the exact prepared roster/options/weapons/stage and cannot rerandomize, quick-team mutate, challenge-strip, or fallibly re-resolve after SVC_STAGE_START serialization. B-1070 owns the contradictory lobby-stage type boundary exposed by production smoke: introduce an exact mode-typed resolver for map versus arena, preserve campaign map-only semantics, and prove both wrong-domain rejection and ordinary two-client lifecycle. B-1071 removes the legacy positional CLC lobby handicap cache and makes each authenticated client settings the exact server-side roster authority, with a protocol bump and final SVC stage roster remaining authoritative. Historical c3746 Cohorts A, B, C, and the narrow E guards remain implemented: checked spawn-critical accessors, one spawn-with-weapon predicate, an exhausted allocation-time struct-field audit, loud body identity rejection, head-count lookup, and bot preload symmetry. The D overlay exists but is not complete. B-1064 owns exact typed identity, atomic player allocation, match participant preparation, chrbody publication, network stage application, and reconnect rollback. B-1065 owns engine-forced option ownership across start/end/cancel/disconnect/settings replacement and user-facing reads. B-1066 owns explicit stage-reuse reset defaults for weapon, previous/dual, ammo intent, passive mode, and jump state. Close with shared prepare/commit contracts, complete rollback, focused behavioral and negative-path tests, and source-frozen ordinary Campaign, Combat Simulator, transition, listen-host/client, disconnect, and reconnect receipts. B-1067 additionally owns prepared-roster drift between lobby commit and launch: exact decline restoration, remote option derivation, participant teams, typed mission identity, and catalog-before-readiness ordering. B-1069 owns the remaining post-freeze launch mutation: network mpStartMatch must consume the exact prepared roster/options/weapons/stage and cannot rerandomize, quick-team mutate, challenge-strip, or fallibly re-resolve after SVC_STAGE_START serialization. B-1070 owns the contradictory lobby-stage type boundary exposed by production smoke: introduce an exact mode-typed resolver for map versus arena, preserve campaign map-only semantics, and prove both wrong-domain rejection and ordinary two-client lifecycle. B-1071 removes the legacy positional CLC lobby handicap cache and makes each authenticated client settings the exact server-side roster authority, with a protocol bump and final SVC stage roster remaining authoritative. B-1071 remediation is source-connected but remains partial until focused builds/tests and a fresh ordinary two-client lifecycle pass under one source freeze. The first v55 ordinary run proved the positional field removal but exposed that transport-complete CLC_SETTINGS was still required. The current source now routes exact typed body/head identity, nonzero handicap, team, options, FOV, and name through a pure transactional codec before roster preparation; B-1071 remains partial until current-source focused/full tests and a source-frozen ordinary two-client lifecycle pass.

B-1072 was exposed by the first rebuilt ordinary-client v55 handshake: mpPlayerSetDefaults cleared gunfuncs[6] with the parent player-config count 16, zeroing the adjacent neutral handicap and pointer bytes. The protocol correctly failed closed before packet publication. Current source scopes the clear to sizeof the exact gunfuncs field and adds a focused boundary pin; rebuild, focused/full tests, source freeze, and ordinary two-client rerun remain required.

B-1073 was exposed only after B-1072 and the complete v55 settings handshake passed: zero-bot CLC_LOBBY_START had asymmetric writer/reader semantics. Current source establishes one canonical no-bot wire form at the shared preparation boundary and aligns UI/automation callers. B-1074 separately corrects stale-loop-variable KillMaster accounting found by the bounded Luna propagation audit. Both remain partial until focused/full build evidence and their ordinary runtime gates pass.

B-1075 was exposed by the otherwise passing B-1071/B-1072/B-1073 two-client receipt: the manifest diff collapsed ASSET_ARENA into MANIFEST_TYPE_STAGE and reconstructed ASSET_MAP, so both processes skipped the exact Felicity typed load while gameplay continued through a separate stage path. The source unit remains partial. Repair must resolve the concrete type from the exact catalog ID, validate that it maps back to the transported token (including generic slot agreement), preserve disabled-row unload classification, cover the parallel audio family, and make the ordinary smoke fail on any mismatch or manifest skip.

B-1075 source verification now passes. One shared pure helper owns concrete-type-to-manifest-category mapping and category acceptance; exact string-ID catalog lookup supplies the concrete type through diff/load/unload; generic entries require an exact explicit type tag; screen manifests carry asset_type_e directly. Transition validation is no longer advisory: every entering typed root loads before old roots release, any failure releases earlier acquisitions in reverse and preserves the previous global baseline, and disabled rows retain exact classification for release. Focused/related/full tests and native-source guard pass on frozen f86d23bb...; production status remains partial until the strengthened ordinary two-client smoke requires two Felicity typed loads and rejects mismatch, skip, rejection, or rollback.

B-1070 owns the contradictory lobby-stage type boundary exposed by production smoke: introduce an exact mode-typed resolver for map versus arena, preserve campaign map-only semantics, and prove both wrong-domain rejection and ordinary two-client lifecycle. B-1071 removes the legacy positional CLC lobby handicap cache and makes each authenticated client settings the exact server-side roster authority, with a protocol bump and final SVC stage roster remaining authoritative. B-1071 remediation is source-connected but remains partial until focused builds/tests and a fresh ordinary two-client lifecycle pass under one source freeze. B-1072 was exposed by the first rebuilt ordinary-client v55 handshake: mpPlayerSetDefaults cleared gunfuncs[6] with the parent player-config count 16, zeroing the adjacent neutral handicap and pointer bytes. The protocol correctly failed closed before packet publication. Current source scopes the clear to sizeof the exact gunfuncs field and adds a focused boundary pin; rebuild, focused/full tests, source freeze, and ordinary two-client rerun remain required.

B-1074 separately corrects stale-loop-variable KillMaster accounting found by the bounded Luna propagation audit. detail.from:
Historical c3746 Cohorts A, B, C, and the narrow E guards remain implemented: checked spawn-critical accessors, one spawn-with-weapon predicate, an exhausted allocation-time struct-field audit, loud body identity rejection, head-count lookup, and bot preload symmetry. The D overlay exists but is not complete. B-1064 owns exact typed identity, atomic player allocation, match participant preparation, chrbody publication, network stage application, and reconnect rollback. B-1065 owns engine-forced option ownership across start/end/cancel/disconnect/settings replacement and user-facing reads. B-1066 owns explicit stage-reuse reset defaults for weapon, previous/dual, ammo intent, passive mode, and jump state. Close with shared prepare/commit contracts, complete rollback, focused behavioral and negative-path tests, and source-frozen ordinary Campaign, Combat Simulator, transition, listen-host/client, disconnect, and reconnect receipts. B-1067 additionally owns prepared-roster drift between lobby commit and launch: exact decline restoration, remote option derivation, participant teams, typed mission identity, and catalog-before-readiness ordering. B-1069 owns the remaining post-freeze launch mutation: network mpStartMatch must consume the exact prepared roster/options/weapons/stage and cannot rerandomize, quick-team mutate, challenge-strip, or fallibly re-resolve after SVC_STAGE_START serialization. B-1070 owns the contradictory lobby-stage type boundary exposed by production smoke: introduce an exact mode-typed resolver for map versus arena, preserve campaign map-only semantics, and prove both wrong-domain rejection and ordinary two-client lifecycle. B-1071 removes the legacy positional CLC lobby handicap cache and makes each authenticated client settings the exact server-side roster authority, with a protocol bump and final SVC stage roster remaining authoritative. B-1071 remediation is source-connected but remains partial until focused builds/tests and a fresh ordinary two-client lifecycle pass under one source freeze. The first v55 ordinary run proved the positional field removal but exposed that transport-complete CLC_SETTINGS was still required. The current source now routes exact typed body/head identity, nonzero handicap, team, options, FOV, and name through a pure transactional codec before roster preparation; B-1071 remains partial until current-source focused/full tests and a source-frozen ordinary two-client lifecycle pass.

B-1072 was exposed by the first rebuilt ordinary-client v55 handshake: mpPlayerSetDefaults cleared gunfuncs[6] with the parent player-config count 16, zeroing the adjacent neutral handicap and pointer bytes. The protocol correctly failed closed before packet publication. Current source scopes the clear to sizeof the exact gunfuncs field and adds a focused boundary pin; rebuild, focused/full tests, source freeze, and ordinary two-client rerun remain required.

B-1073 was exposed only after B-1072 and the complete v55 settings handshake passed: zero-bot CLC_LOBBY_START had asymmetric writer/reader semantics. Current source establishes one canonical no-bot wire form at the shared preparation boundary and aligns UI/automation callers. B-1074 separately corrects stale-loop-variable KillMaster accounting found by the bounded Luna propagation audit. Both remain partial until focused/full build evidence and their ordinary runtime gates pass.

B-1075 was exposed by the otherwise passing B-1071/B-1072/B-1073 two-client receipt: the manifest diff collapsed ASSET_ARENA into MANIFEST_TYPE_STAGE and reconstructed ASSET_MAP, so both processes skipped the exact Felicity typed load while gameplay continued through a separate stage path. The source unit remains partial. Repair must resolve the concrete type from the exact catalog ID, validate that it maps back to the transported token (including generic slot agreement), preserve disabled-row unload classification, cover the parallel audio family, and make the ordinary smoke fail on any mismatch or manifest skip.

B-1075 source verification now passes. One shared pure helper owns concrete-type-to-manifest-category mapping and category acceptance; exact string-ID catalog lookup supplies the concrete type through diff/load/unload; generic entries require an exact explicit type tag; screen manifests carry asset_type_e directly. Transition validation is no longer advisory: every entering typed root loads before old roots release, any failure releases earlier acquisitions in reverse and preserves the previous global baseline, and disabled rows retain exact classification for release. Focused/related/full tests and native-source guard pass on frozen f86d23bb...; production status remains partial until the strengthened ordinary two-client smoke requires two Felicity typed loads and rejects mismatch, skip, rejection, or rollback.

The strengthened source-frozen ordinary two-client rerun is accepted: results-20260813T091851Z.json passes 56/56, both processes perform the exact typed Felicity manifest load, and no mismatch, load skip, transition rejection/rollback, crash, or fatal signature appears. B-1070, B-1071, B-1072, B-1073, and B-1075 therefore move to implementation-complete regression gates on this frozen unit. T-ENGINE-004 remains partial: B-1074 still needs controlled non-tied award totals, and the task still requires ordinary Campaign, repeated Combat Simulator return/restart, transition reset, disconnect/reconnect, both D-003 authority cases, and V-009 visual regression proof before validation.

Post-receipt warning triage kept markerless Felicity spawn-with-weapon fallback, rejected L1 pads with complete later L1 coverage, and the guarded zero-FOV clamp out of the defect count. The current body86/head4 missing-headspot warning strengthens B-183. B-1076 is newly confirmed: the host reaches match startup with an orphaned non-optional agent_select pool slot and succeeds only because menuPoolConsistencyCheck bulk-releases it. The repeated ordinary Combat Simulator cycle must now prove the owning close transaction and forbid watchdog repair.

B-1077 corrective runtime evidence disproved the earlier upper-floor hypothesis: canonical collision and mesh queries both returned floor y=0, while the hook incorrectly compared that floor to player prop y=159. Current source uses vv_ground. B-1078 routes delayed match-end saves through atomic PC-native Agent Profile/MP-player JSON and the corrective smoke proves the endscreen stays at depth 1 through the real Play Again edge. That same receipt exposed B-1079: a bootstrap-seeded match config was reset on first Room render, losing arena, roster, and options. Current source adds an explicit adopt-existing-config boundary on solo return. All three remain partial until the next source-frozen two-cycle ordinary-client receipt passes natural visibility/hit, exact setup preservation, awards, and second endscreen.

The next source-frozen diagnostic remains rejected, but it narrows B-1077 further: floor selection and cached-ground metadata were correct, while the smoke helper incorrectly used the floor as the actor-root Y. The canonical character tick then sampled Chicago's upper step and moved the bot before visibility. Current source preserves the standing actor-root height and passes selected floor metadata separately. The fixture is restored to a 200-second two-cycle exit and explicitly requires exactly one cold MATCHSETUP init plus one Room adoption marker. Rebuild, focused tests, and the complete ordinary-client receipt remain required.

The restored 200-second source-frozen Combat Simulator gate now reaches both complete cycles and is rejected at 52/54 solely because the naturally fired CMP150 shots miss. This promotes B-1074, B-1078, and B-1079 to regression gates: controlled awards pass twice, the native save and real Play Again route reach cycle two without Pak UI/watchdog repair, and one explicit Room adoption preserves the exact user setup with only one cold MATCHSETUP initialization. B-1077 remains confirmed rather than implemented. Floor selection and cached-ground publication are correct, but the ordinary actor update between placement and culling rewrites y=159 to y=697. The current critical path is a teleport-safe action/animation state applied before the canonical actor tick, followed by a source-frozen 54/54 rerun; no synthetic visibility or hit is acceptable.

Historical c3746 Cohorts A, B, C, and the narrow E guards remain implemented: checked spawn-critical accessors, one spawn-with-weapon predicate, an exhausted allocation-time struct-field audit, loud body identity rejection, head-count lookup, and bot preload symmetry. The D overlay exists but is not complete. B-1064 owns exact typed identity, atomic player allocation, match participant preparation, chrbody publication, network stage application, and reconnect rollback. B-1065 owns engine-forced option ownership across start/end/cancel/disconnect/settings replacement and user-facing reads. B-1066 owns explicit stage-reuse reset defaults for weapon, previous/dual, ammo intent, passive mode, and jump state. Close with shared prepare/commit contracts, complete rollback, focused behavioral and negative-path tests, and source-frozen ordinary Campaign, Combat Simulator, transition, listen-host/client, disconnect, and reconnect receipts. B-1067 additionally owns prepared-roster drift between lobby commit and launch: exact decline restoration, remote option derivation, participant teams, typed mission identity, and catalog-before-readiness ordering. B-1069 owns the remaining post-freeze launch mutation: network mpStartMatch must consume the exact prepared roster/options/weapons/stage and cannot rerandomize, quick-team mutate, challenge-strip, or fallibly re-resolve after SVC_STAGE_START serialization. B-1070 owns the contradictory lobby-stage type boundary exposed by production smoke: introduce an exact mode-typed resolver for map versus arena, preserve campaign map-only semantics, and prove both wrong-domain rejection and ordinary two-client lifecycle. B-1071 removes the legacy positional CLC lobby handicap cache and makes each authenticated client settings the exact server-side roster authority, with a protocol bump and final SVC stage roster remaining authoritative. B-1071 remediation is source-connected but remains partial until focused builds/tests and a fresh ordinary two-client lifecycle pass under one source freeze. The first v55 ordinary run proved the positional field removal but exposed that transport-complete CLC_SETTINGS was still required. The current source now routes exact typed body/head identity, nonzero handicap, team, options, FOV, and name through a pure transactional codec before roster preparation; B-1071 remains partial until current-source focused/full tests and a source-frozen ordinary two-client lifecycle pass.

B-1072 was exposed by the first rebuilt ordinary-client v55 handshake: mpPlayerSetDefaults cleared gunfuncs[6] with the parent player-config count 16, zeroing the adjacent neutral handicap and pointer bytes. The protocol correctly failed closed before packet publication. Current source scopes the clear to sizeof the exact gunfuncs field and adds a focused boundary pin; rebuild, focused/full tests, source freeze, and ordinary two-client rerun remain required.

B-1073 was exposed only after B-1072 and the complete v55 settings handshake passed: zero-bot CLC_LOBBY_START had asymmetric writer/reader semantics. Current source establishes one canonical no-bot wire form at the shared preparation boundary and aligns UI/automation callers. B-1074 separately corrects stale-loop-variable KillMaster accounting found by the bounded Luna propagation audit. Both remain partial until focused/full build evidence and their ordinary runtime gates pass.

B-1075 was exposed by the otherwise passing B-1071/B-1072/B-1073 two-client receipt: the manifest diff collapsed ASSET_ARENA into MANIFEST_TYPE_STAGE and reconstructed ASSET_MAP, so both processes skipped the exact Felicity typed load while gameplay continued through a separate stage path. The source unit remains partial. Repair must resolve the concrete type from the exact catalog ID, validate that it maps back to the transported token (including generic slot agreement), preserve disabled-row unload classification, cover the parallel audio family, and make the ordinary smoke fail on any mismatch or manifest skip.

B-1075 source verification now passes. One shared pure helper owns concrete-type-to-manifest-category mapping and category acceptance; exact string-ID catalog lookup supplies the concrete type through diff/load/unload; generic entries require an exact explicit type tag; screen manifests carry asset_type_e directly. Transition validation is no longer advisory: every entering typed root loads before old roots release, any failure releases earlier acquisitions in reverse and preserves the previous global baseline, and disabled rows retain exact classification for release. Focused/related/full tests and native-source guard pass on frozen f86d23bb...; production status remains partial until the strengthened ordinary two-client smoke requires two Felicity typed loads and rejects mismatch, skip, rejection, or rollback.

The strengthened source-frozen ordinary two-client rerun is accepted: results-20260813T091851Z.json passes 56/56, both processes perform the exact typed Felicity manifest load, and no mismatch, load skip, transition rejection/rollback, crash, or fatal signature appears. B-1070, B-1071, B-1072, B-1073, and B-1075 therefore move to implementation-complete regression gates on this frozen unit. T-ENGINE-004 remains partial: B-1074 still needs controlled non-tied award totals, and the task still requires ordinary Campaign, repeated Combat Simulator return/restart, transition reset, disconnect/reconnect, both D-003 authority cases, and V-009 visual regression proof before validation.

Post-receipt warning triage kept markerless Felicity spawn-with-weapon fallback, rejected L1 pads with complete later L1 coverage, and the guarded zero-FOV clamp out of the defect count. The current body86/head4 missing-headspot warning strengthens B-183. B-1076 is newly confirmed: the host reaches match startup with an orphaned non-optional agent_select pool slot and succeeds only because menuPoolConsistencyCheck bulk-releases it. The repeated ordinary Combat Simulator cycle must now prove the owning close transaction and forbid watchdog repair.

B-1077 corrective runtime evidence disproved the earlier upper-floor hypothesis: canonical collision and mesh queries both returned floor y=0, while the hook incorrectly compared that floor to player prop y=159. Current source uses vv_ground. B-1078 routes delayed match-end saves through atomic PC-native Agent Profile/MP-player JSON and the corrective smoke proves the endscreen stays at depth 1 through the real Play Again edge. That same receipt exposed B-1079: a bootstrap-seeded match config was reset on first Room render, losing arena, roster, and options. Current source adds an explicit adopt-existing-config boundary on solo return. All three remain partial until the next source-frozen two-cycle ordinary-client receipt passes natural visibility/hit, exact setup preservation, awards, and second endscreen.

The next source-frozen diagnostic remains rejected, but it narrows B-1077 further: floor selection and cached-ground metadata were correct, while the smoke helper incorrectly used the floor as the actor-root Y. The canonical character tick then sampled Chicago's upper step and moved the bot before visibility. Current source preserves the standing actor-root height and passes selected floor metadata separately. The fixture is restored to a 200-second two-cycle exit and explicitly requires exactly one cold MATCHSETUP init plus one Room adoption marker. Rebuild, focused tests, and the complete ordinary-client receipt remain required.

The restored 200-second source-frozen Combat Simulator gate now reaches both complete cycles and is rejected at 52/54 solely because the naturally fired CMP150 shots miss. This promotes B-1074, B-1078, and B-1079 to regression gates: controlled awards pass twice, the native save and real Play Again route reach cycle two without Pak UI/watchdog repair, and one explicit Room adoption preserves the exact user setup with only one cold MATCHSETUP initialization. B-1077 remains confirmed rather than implemented. Floor selection and cached-ground publication are correct, but the ordinary actor update between placement and culling rewrites y=159 to y=697. The current critical path is a teleport-safe action/animation state applied before the canonical actor tick, followed by a source-frozen 54/54 rerun; no synthetic visibility or hit is acceptable.

B-1077 root cause is now structurally fixed in current source: the ordinary character tick reconstructed world Y from stale CHRINFO animation endpoints after a root-plus-ground relocation. One model-layer actor relocation primitive now rebases all ordinary active/merge Y anchors by the exact ground-relative root delta while preserving authored absolute-translation Y, and the production magic-nav, cached-ground teleport, adjusted move, and surface-locomotion paths use it. Isolated focused verification passes 915 assertions/10 player-init cases and 1,296 assertions/16 external-model cases. B-1077 and T-ENGINE-004 remain partial until a rebuilt source-frozen two-cycle ordinary-client receipt passes all 54 assertions with natural cull/sort/render inclusion and a real hit.

Isolated focused verification passes 915 assertions/10 player-init cases and 1,296 assertions/16 external-model cases. B-1077 and T-ENGINE-004 remain partial until a rebuilt source-frozen two-cycle ordinary-client receipt passes all 54 assertions with natural cull/sort/render inclusion and a real hit.

B-1080 is now the current critical blocker. B-1077's specific relocation invariant reached natural cull and sort at y=159, exposing an unbounded generated-character GDL walk in bgTestHitOnChr before the first real shot. Generated payloads retain byte lengths but the hit-test boundary receives only raw pointers. The structural fix must expose exact registered GDL spans, bound both hit streams, fail closed on malformed or unowned generated lists without synthesizing a hit, retain a safe native-list guard, and pass focused/full tests plus the source-frozen two-cycle ordinary-client gate. T-ENGINE-004 remains partial.

B-1067 additionally owns prepared-roster drift between lobby commit and launch: exact decline restoration, remote option derivation, participant teams, typed mission identity, and catalog-before-readiness ordering. B-1070 owns the contradictory lobby-stage type boundary exposed by production smoke: introduce an exact mode-typed resolver for map versus arena, preserve campaign map-only semantics, and prove both wrong-domain rejection and ordinary two-client lifecycle. B-1071 removes the legacy positional CLC lobby handicap cache and makes each authenticated client settings the exact server-side roster authority, with a protocol bump and final SVC stage roster remaining authoritative. B-1071 remediation is source-connected but remains partial until focused builds/tests and a fresh ordinary two-client lifecycle pass under one source freeze. The first v55 ordinary run proved the positional field removal but exposed that transport-complete CLC_SETTINGS was still required. The current source now routes exact typed body/head identity, nonzero handicap, team, options, FOV, and name through a pure transactional codec before roster preparation; B-1071 remains partial until current-source focused/full tests and a source-frozen ordinary two-client lifecycle pass.

B-1072 was exposed by the first rebuilt ordinary-client v55 handshake: mpPlayerSetDefaults cleared gunfuncs[6] with the parent player-config count 16, zeroing the adjacent neutral handicap and pointer bytes. The protocol correctly failed closed before packet publication. Current source scopes the clear to sizeof the exact gunfuncs field and adds a focused boundary pin; rebuild, focused/full tests, source freeze, and ordinary two-client rerun remain required.

B-1073 was exposed only after B-1072 and the complete v55 settings handshake passed: zero-bot CLC_LOBBY_START had asymmetric writer/reader semantics. Current source establishes one canonical no-bot wire form at the shared preparation boundary and aligns UI/automation callers. B-1074 separately corrects stale-loop-variable KillMaster accounting found by the bounded Luna propagation audit. detail.from:
Historical c3746 guards and the B-1064 through B-1085 architecture are source-connected: exact typed player identity, candidate-first roster/stage/manifest preparation, authenticated protocol-v55 client settings, immutable network launch consumption, engine-forced option ownership, explicit stage-reuse defaults, PC-native delayed-save ownership, Room rematch adoption, generated-character floor/root relocation, exact generated-GDL traversal bounds, and finite fixture-owned diagnostics.

The accepted current runtime baseline passes a bounded 13/13 generated-audit diagnostic, a diagnostics-disabled 56/56 two-cycle ordinary Combat Simulator fixture, and the source-frozen 145/145 initiator-authority friend-play fixture. Together they prove stable generated-character placement, natural hit traversal, awards/stats persistence, native save, real Play Again return, setup preservation, two complete endscreens, exactly one authority-first listen startup plus typed signed route plus idempotent join, Needler gameplay/presentation witnesses, and clean exits. The prior full pd-tests suite passed 59,094 assertions in 1,117 cases and the public native-source guard passed.

B-1084 is a regression gate. The source-frozen invitee-authority receipt passes D-003 election, one in-client ENet listen bind, separately typed signed-route publication, one idempotent join, package transfer, manifest readiness, two-player immutable stage start, cutscene exit, and Needler model load. It remains rejected at 138/144 solely because B-1085 prevents the background authority from consuming smoke-owned injected gameplay input: injection mutates ActionState, but public reads still apply the production focus suppression gate. Current source implements explicit held/release ownership and a player-aware read gate that bypasses only focus-loss/regain settling under Gameplay or Forge; physical dispatch, analog polling, typed layers, menus, freefly, flush, and release-edge cleanup remain authoritative. The isolated build passes; focused B-1085/input-layer contracts pass 59 assertions in 5 cases, D-003 passes 119/5, full automation passes 59,149/1,118, and the native-source guard passes on the 3,092-file `5cd19966...` unit. Both-role runtime verification remains pending.

T-ENGINE-004 remains partial. Closure still requires B-1085 focused/full verification and both current-source authority reruns, ordinary Campaign/player-init, all-17-mission/restart regression, stage-transition reset, strengthened listen-host/client lifecycle, disconnect/reconnect, D-003 failure rollback, and a gameplay capture retaining V-009 visual gates. Receipts with source overlap, stale binaries, early termination, diagnostic-only behavior, or missing assertions remain rejected.

detail.from:
Historical c3746 guards and the B-1064 through B-1085 architecture are source-connected: exact typed player identity, candidate-first roster/stage/manifest preparation, authenticated protocol-v55 client settings, immutable network launch consumption, engine-forced option ownership, explicit stage-reuse defaults, PC-native delayed-save ownership, Room rematch adoption, generated-character floor/root relocation, exact generated-GDL traversal bounds, and finite fixture-owned diagnostics.

The accepted current runtime baseline passes a bounded 13/13 generated-audit diagnostic, a diagnostics-disabled 56/56 two-cycle ordinary Combat Simulator fixture, and the source-frozen 145/145 initiator-authority friend-play fixture. Together they prove stable generated-character placement, natural hit traversal, awards/stats persistence, native save, real Play Again return, setup preservation, two complete endscreens, exactly one authority-first listen startup plus typed signed route plus idempotent join, Needler gameplay/presentation witnesses, and clean exits. The prior full pd-tests suite passed 59,094 assertions in 1,117 cases and the public native-source guard passed.

B-1084 is a regression gate. The source-frozen invitee-authority receipt passes D-003 election, one in-client ENet listen bind, separately typed signed-route publication, one idempotent join, package transfer, manifest readiness, two-player immutable stage start, cutscene exit, and Needler model load. It remains rejected at 138/144 solely because B-1085 prevents the background authority from consuming smoke-owned injected gameplay input: injection mutates ActionState, but public reads still apply the production focus suppression gate. Current source implements explicit held/release ownership and a player-aware read gate that bypasses only focus-loss/regain settling under Gameplay or Forge; physical dispatch, analog polling, typed layers, menus, freefly, flush, and release-edge cleanup remain authoritative. The first ownership revision passed build, focused 59/5, D-003 119/5, full 59,149/1,118, and the native-source guard on `5cd19966...`, but Luna xhigh review found physical axis overwrite and coincident physical-edge ownership gaps before runtime; that binary is superseded. Current source routes all physical axis writes/zeroing through an ownership-aware setter, makes fireVk defer before mutation for the exact owned action, and strengthens function-scoped contracts. Corrected-source build/focused/full/guard and both-role runtime verification are pending.

T-ENGINE-004 remains partial. Closure still requires B-1085 focused/full verification and both current-source authority reruns, ordinary Campaign/player-init, all-17-mission/restart regression, stage-transition reset, strengthened listen-host/client lifecycle, disconnect/reconnect, D-003 failure rollback, and a gameplay capture retaining V-009 visual gates. Receipts with source overlap, stale binaries, early termination, diagnostic-only behavior, or missing assertions remain rejected.

Historical c3746 guards and the B-1064 through B-1085 architecture are source-connected: exact typed player identity, candidate-first roster/stage/manifest preparation, authenticated protocol-v55 client settings, immutable network launch consumption, engine-forced option ownership, explicit stage-reuse defaults, PC-native delayed-save ownership, Room rematch adoption, generated-character floor/root relocation, exact generated-GDL traversal bounds, and finite fixture-owned diagnostics.

The accepted current runtime baseline passes a bounded 13/13 generated-audit diagnostic, a diagnostics-disabled 56/56 two-cycle ordinary Combat Simulator fixture, and the source-frozen 145/145 initiator-authority friend-play fixture. Together they prove stable generated-character placement, natural hit traversal, awards/stats persistence, native save, real Play Again return, setup preservation, two complete endscreens, exactly one authority-first listen startup plus typed signed route plus idempotent join, Needler gameplay/presentation witnesses, and clean exits. The prior full pd-tests suite passed 59,094 assertions in 1,117 cases and the public native-source guard passed.

B-1084 is a regression gate. The source-frozen invitee-authority receipt passes D-003 election, one in-client ENet listen bind, separately typed signed-route publication, one idempotent join, package transfer, manifest readiness, two-player immutable stage start, cutscene exit, and Needler model load. It remains rejected at 138/144 solely because B-1085 prevents the background authority from consuming smoke-owned injected gameplay input: injection mutates ActionState, but public reads still apply the production focus suppression gate. Current source implements explicit held/release ownership and a player-aware read gate that bypasses only focus-loss/regain settling under Gameplay or Forge; physical dispatch, analog polling, typed layers, menus, freefly, flush, and release-edge cleanup remain authoritative. The first ownership revision passed build, focused 59/5, D-003 119/5, full 59,149/1,118, and the native-source guard on `5cd19966...`, but Luna xhigh review found physical axis overwrite and coincident physical-edge ownership gaps before runtime; that binary is superseded. Current source routes all physical axis writes/zeroing through an ownership-aware setter, makes fireVk defer before mutation for the exact owned action, and strengthens function-scoped contracts. The corrected `8be06c29...` unit passes build, B-1085/input-layer 111/5, D-003 119/5, full 59,201/1,118, and the native-source guard; exact client `DB92FB2F...`, tests `1017E05A...`, updater `C7446779...`. Both-role runtime verification remains pending.

T-ENGINE-004 remains partial. Closure still requires B-1085 focused/full verification and both current-source authority reruns, ordinary Campaign/player-init, all-17-mission/restart regression, stage-transition reset, strengthened listen-host/client lifecycle, disconnect/reconnect, D-003 failure rollback, and a gameplay capture retaining V-009 visual gates. Receipts with source overlap, stale binaries, early termination, diagnostic-only behavior, or missing assertions remain rejected.

detail.from:
Historical c3746 guards and the B-1064 through B-1085 architecture are source-connected: exact typed player identity, candidate-first roster/stage/manifest preparation, authenticated protocol-v55 client settings, immutable network launch consumption, engine-forced option ownership, explicit stage-reuse defaults, PC-native delayed-save ownership, Room rematch adoption, generated-character floor/root relocation, exact generated-GDL traversal bounds, and finite fixture-owned diagnostics.

The accepted current runtime baseline passes a bounded 13/13 generated-audit diagnostic, a diagnostics-disabled 56/56 two-cycle ordinary Combat Simulator fixture, and the source-frozen 145/145 initiator-authority friend-play fixture. Together they prove stable generated-character placement, natural hit traversal, awards/stats persistence, native save, real Play Again return, setup preservation, two complete endscreens, exactly one authority-first listen startup plus typed signed route plus idempotent join, Needler gameplay/presentation witnesses, and clean exits. The prior full pd-tests suite passed 59,094 assertions in 1,117 cases and the public native-source guard passed.

B-1084 is a regression gate. The source-frozen invitee-authority receipt passes D-003 election, one in-client ENet listen bind, separately typed signed-route publication, one idempotent join, package transfer, manifest readiness, two-player immutable stage start, cutscene exit, and Needler model load. It remains rejected at 138/144 solely because B-1085 prevents the background authority from consuming smoke-owned injected gameplay input: injection mutates ActionState, but public reads still apply the production focus suppression gate. Current source implements explicit held/release ownership and a player-aware read gate that bypasses only focus-loss/regain settling under Gameplay or Forge; physical dispatch, analog polling, typed layers, menus, freefly, flush, and release-edge cleanup remain authoritative. The first ownership revision passed build, focused 59/5, D-003 119/5, full 59,149/1,118, and the native-source guard on `5cd19966...`, but Luna xhigh review found physical axis overwrite and coincident physical-edge ownership gaps before runtime; that binary is superseded. Current source routes all physical axis writes/zeroing through an ownership-aware setter, makes fireVk defer before mutation for the exact owned action, and strengthens function-scoped contracts. The corrected `8be06c29...` unit passes build, B-1085/input-layer 111/5, D-003 119/5, full 59,201/1,118, and the native-source guard; exact client `DB92FB2F...`, tests `1017E05A...`, updater `C7446779...`. Both-role runtime verification remains pending.

T-ENGINE-004 remains partial. Closure still requires B-1085 focused/full verification and both current-source authority reruns, ordinary Campaign/player-init, all-17-mission/restart regression, stage-transition reset, strengthened listen-host/client lifecycle, disconnect/reconnect, D-003 failure rollback, and a gameplay capture retaining V-009 visual gates. Receipts with source overlap, stale binaries, early termination, diagnostic-only behavior, or missing assertions remain rejected.

The first corrected invitee rerun passed all 144 existing assertions, but it remains partial rather than B-1085 closure because those assertions could succeed without proving focus loss, smoke ownership, and the gameplay read path; the run also omitted retained raw logs. The invitee-process fixture now requires all three witnesses. A retained-log invitee rerun and then initiator-authority rerun on the same source freeze remain pending.

The retained strengthened invitee run proves the owned fire and gameplay read path but is rejected at 146/147 because process launch did not produce a deterministic focus transition. The verifier must focus the declared source process, then the target process, and wait fail-closed for the source log witness before the smoke can exercise B-1085 intentionally.

The generic deterministic focus verifier is source-connected and passes focused, D-003, full-suite, native-source, AST, JSON, and C# interop compilation gates on candidate freeze `4257975d...`. The invitee and initiator ordinary-client reruns remain pending; candidate evidence is not runtime acceptance.

detail.from:
Historical c3746 guards and the B-1064 through B-1085 architecture are source-connected: exact typed player identity, candidate-first roster/stage/manifest preparation, authenticated protocol-v55 client settings, immutable network launch consumption, engine-forced option ownership, explicit stage-reuse defaults, PC-native delayed-save ownership, Room rematch adoption, generated-character floor/root relocation, exact generated-GDL traversal bounds, and finite fixture-owned diagnostics.

The accepted current runtime baseline passes a bounded 13/13 generated-audit diagnostic, a diagnostics-disabled 56/56 two-cycle ordinary Combat Simulator fixture, and the source-frozen 145/145 initiator-authority friend-play fixture. Together they prove stable generated-character placement, natural hit traversal, awards/stats persistence, native save, real Play Again return, setup preservation, two complete endscreens, exactly one authority-first listen startup plus typed signed route plus idempotent join, Needler gameplay/presentation witnesses, and clean exits. The prior full pd-tests suite passed 59,094 assertions in 1,117 cases and the public native-source guard passed.

B-1084 is a regression gate. The source-frozen invitee-authority receipt passes D-003 election, one in-client ENet listen bind, separately typed signed-route publication, one idempotent join, package transfer, manifest readiness, two-player immutable stage start, cutscene exit, and Needler model load. It remains rejected at 138/144 solely because B-1085 prevents the background authority from consuming smoke-owned injected gameplay input: injection mutates ActionState, but public reads still apply the production focus suppression gate. Current source implements explicit held/release ownership and a player-aware read gate that bypasses only focus-loss/regain settling under Gameplay or Forge; physical dispatch, analog polling, typed layers, menus, freefly, flush, and release-edge cleanup remain authoritative. The first ownership revision passed build, focused 59/5, D-003 119/5, full 59,149/1,118, and the native-source guard on `5cd19966...`, but Luna xhigh review found physical axis overwrite and coincident physical-edge ownership gaps before runtime; that binary is superseded. Current source routes all physical axis writes/zeroing through an ownership-aware setter, makes fireVk defer before mutation for the exact owned action, and strengthens function-scoped contracts. The corrected `8be06c29...` unit passes build, B-1085/input-layer 111/5, D-003 119/5, full 59,201/1,118, and the native-source guard; exact client `DB92FB2F...`, tests `1017E05A...`, updater `C7446779...`. Both-role runtime verification remains pending.

T-ENGINE-004 remains partial. Closure still requires B-1085 focused/full verification and both current-source authority reruns, ordinary Campaign/player-init, all-17-mission/restart regression, stage-transition reset, strengthened listen-host/client lifecycle, disconnect/reconnect, D-003 failure rollback, and a gameplay capture retaining V-009 visual gates. Receipts with source overlap, stale binaries, early termination, diagnostic-only behavior, or missing assertions remain rejected.

The first corrected invitee rerun passed all 144 existing assertions, but it remains partial rather than B-1085 closure because those assertions could succeed without proving focus loss, smoke ownership, and the gameplay read path; the run also omitted retained raw logs. The invitee-process fixture now requires all three witnesses. A retained-log invitee rerun and then initiator-authority rerun on the same source freeze remain pending.

The retained strengthened invitee run proves the owned fire and gameplay read path but is rejected at 146/147 because process launch did not produce a deterministic focus transition. The verifier must focus the declared source process, then the target process, and wait fail-closed for the source log witness before the smoke can exercise B-1085 intentionally.

The generic deterministic focus verifier is source-connected and passes focused, D-003, full-suite, native-source, AST, JSON, and C# interop compilation gates on candidate freeze `4257975d...`. The invitee and initiator ordinary-client reruns remain pending; candidate evidence is not runtime acceptance.
The first deterministic-focus attempt is rejected at 62/147: focus orchestration began only after the invitee readiness barrier, while the first-launch initiator was still extracting and had no SDL window. The fixture now requires both named readiness markers. Luna's second xhigh review then found that unordered presence checks could still combine a focus loss with an earlier fire pulse. Current source adds a generic strict ordered-sequence assertion family, append-only log freshness, target-foreground revalidation, full timeout-bound focus acquisition, an exact clean owner-acquisition witness, and a production-linked pure action-read authority seam with native unowned focus-loss denial. Smoke release can no longer seize or mutate unowned physical state. These changes pass PowerShell AST, fixture JSON, C# interop compilation, and assertion-engine behavioral self-tests; compiled and ordinary-client evidence remain pending.
The causal-authority revision now compiles in both shipping client and pd-tests. On an unchanged 6bd8d3ec.../3104-file source fingerprint, focused B-1085/action authority passes 316/28, canonical D-003 passes 167/6, the full suite passes 59,297/1,124, the ordered assertion self-test passes, and the native-source guard passes. Exact candidate hashes are client 77E869A6..., tests 07BC22CB..., updater C7446779.... Luna follow-up and both retained ordinary-client authority roles remain pending, so this is compiled partial evidence rather than B-1085 closure.

Historical c3746 guards and the B-1064 through B-1085 architecture are source-connected: exact typed player identity, candidate-first roster/stage/manifest preparation, authenticated protocol-v55 client settings, immutable network launch consumption, engine-forced option ownership, explicit stage-reuse defaults, PC-native delayed-save ownership, Room rematch adoption, generated-character floor/root relocation, exact generated-GDL traversal bounds, and finite fixture-owned diagnostics.

The accepted current runtime baseline passes a bounded 13/13 generated-audit diagnostic, a diagnostics-disabled 56/56 two-cycle ordinary Combat Simulator fixture, and the source-frozen 145/145 initiator-authority friend-play fixture. Together they prove stable generated-character placement, natural hit traversal, awards/stats persistence, native save, real Play Again return, setup preservation, two complete endscreens, exactly one authority-first listen startup plus typed signed route plus idempotent join, Needler gameplay/presentation witnesses, and clean exits. The prior full pd-tests suite passed 59,094 assertions in 1,117 cases and the public native-source guard passed.

B-1084 is a regression gate. The source-frozen invitee-authority receipt passes D-003 election, one in-client ENet listen bind, separately typed signed-route publication, one idempotent join, package transfer, manifest readiness, two-player immutable stage start, cutscene exit, and Needler model load. It remains rejected at 138/144 solely because B-1085 prevents the background authority from consuming smoke-owned injected gameplay input: injection mutates ActionState, but public reads still apply the production focus suppression gate. Current source implements explicit held/release ownership and a player-aware read gate that bypasses only focus-loss/regain settling under Gameplay or Forge; physical dispatch, analog polling, typed layers, menus, freefly, flush, and release-edge cleanup remain authoritative. The first ownership revision passed build, focused 59/5, D-003 119/5, full 59,149/1,118, and the native-source guard on `5cd19966...`, but Luna xhigh review found physical axis overwrite and coincident physical-edge ownership gaps before runtime; that binary is superseded. Current source routes all physical axis writes/zeroing through an ownership-aware setter, makes fireVk defer before mutation for the exact owned action, and strengthens function-scoped contracts. The corrected `8be06c29...` unit passes build, B-1085/input-layer 111/5, D-003 119/5, full 59,201/1,118, and the native-source guard; exact client `DB92FB2F...`, tests `1017E05A...`, updater `C7446779...`. Both-role runtime verification remains pending.

T-ENGINE-004 remains partial. Closure still requires B-1085 focused/full verification and both current-source authority reruns, ordinary Campaign/player-init, all-17-mission/restart regression, stage-transition reset, strengthened listen-host/client lifecycle, disconnect/reconnect, D-003 failure rollback, and a gameplay capture retaining V-009 visual gates. Receipts with source overlap, stale binaries, early termination, diagnostic-only behavior, or missing assertions remain rejected.

The first corrected invitee rerun passed all 144 existing assertions, but it remains partial rather than B-1085 closure because those assertions could succeed without proving focus loss, smoke ownership, and the gameplay read path; the run also omitted retained raw logs. The invitee-process fixture now requires all three witnesses. A retained-log invitee rerun and then initiator-authority rerun on the same source freeze remain pending.

The retained strengthened invitee run proves the owned fire and gameplay read path but is rejected at 146/147 because process launch did not produce a deterministic focus transition. The verifier must focus the declared source process, then the target process, and wait fail-closed for the source log witness before the smoke can exercise B-1085 intentionally.

The generic deterministic focus verifier is source-connected and passes focused, D-003, full-suite, native-source, AST, JSON, and C# interop compilation gates on candidate freeze `4257975d...`. The invitee and initiator ordinary-client reruns remain pending; candidate evidence is not runtime acceptance.
The first deterministic-focus attempt is rejected at 62/147: focus orchestration began only after the invitee readiness barrier, while the first-launch initiator was still extracting and had no SDL window. The fixture now requires both named readiness markers. Luna's second xhigh review then found that unordered presence checks could still combine a focus loss with an earlier fire pulse. Current source adds a generic strict ordered-sequence assertion family, append-only log freshness, target-foreground revalidation, full timeout-bound focus acquisition, an exact clean owner-acquisition witness, and a production-linked pure action-read authority seam with native unowned focus-loss denial. Smoke release can no longer seize or mutate unowned physical state. These changes pass PowerShell AST, fixture JSON, C# interop compilation, and assertion-engine behavioral self-tests; compiled and ordinary-client evidence remain pending.
The causal-authority revision now compiles in both shipping client and pd-tests. On an unchanged 6bd8d3ec.../3104-file source fingerprint, focused B-1085/action authority passes 316/28, canonical D-003 passes 167/6, the full suite passes 59,297/1,124, the ordered assertion self-test passes, and the native-source guard passes. Exact candidate hashes are client 77E869A6..., tests 07BC22CB..., updater C7446779.... Luna follow-up and both retained ordinary-client authority roles remain pending, so this is compiled partial evidence rather than B-1085 closure.

The next invitee-authority attempt was rejected before any client launched because a stale typed catalog ID had been placed in remove_paths and could not be resolved as a Windows filesystem path. B-1087 removes that entry from every affected fixture and adds repository-wide path lint. Luna then found an exact-deadline fail-open race in the new readiness harness; current B-1085 source gives pending taps and wait/overall deadlines priority over success or scripted exit, invalidates readiness on stage teardown, and requires strict wait-budget headroom. Both authority fixtures now reserve 60 seconds beyond their 300-second worst-case schedule. This revision is unbuilt, so T-ENGINE-004 remains partial.

The first consolidated both-role runtime batch was stopped after the initiator-authority case exposed B-1088. Route authority, listen startup, typed signed route consumption, one join, package readiness, and two-player stage start all occurred, but presentation timing legitimately diverged: one peer had already reached gameplay while the fixture still demanded the cutscene-only aperture. That wait timed out and disconnected the other peer. No result JSON is accepted. Current source replaces the rigid branch with a pure skip-or-gameplay transition and gates the Skip press on the exact cutscene predicate; release remains unconditional. This revision is structurally checked but unbuilt, so status remains partial.
